facts.statement: Porphyrio claytongreenei was described by Worthy and colleagues.
The species lived during the Pleistocene epoch.
Fossils of Porphyrio claytongreenei have been found in New Zealand.
Porphyrio claytongreenei is classified as a type of swamphen.
Porphyrio claytongreenei belongs to the genus Porphyrio.
The specific epithet of the species is claytongreenei.
Worthy et al. named Porphyrio claytongreenei in 2026.
This extinct rail lived in Zealandia during the Calabrian stage of the Pleistocene.
facts.quote: Porphyrio claytongreenei is an extinct species of rail in the genus Porphyrio that lived in Zealandia during the Calabrian stage of the Pleistocene Epoch.

facts.statement: The name claytongreenei honors Warren Clayton-Greene, the landowner where the holotype was discovered.
facts.quote: The specific epithet of Porphyrio claytongreenei references Warren Clayton-Greene, the landowner of the site on which the holotype was found

facts.statement: Clayton-Greene was honored for protecting fossil sites on his land by fencing them off from livestock.
facts.quote: for his encouragement of scientific research in the caves located on his land and his protection of fossil sites by fencing them off from livestock.

facts.statement: The genus Porphyrio belongs to the family Rallidae.
